situation.problem_text:
Topic: Dot Products and the Concept of Duality

Target audience: University students (Linear Algebra/Engineering)

Section: section_1 — Geometric Intuition: The Projection

Lecture lines:
The dot product measures the projection of vectors.
Visualize it as a shadow cast by light.
It captures how much vectors align together.
Think of a hiker climbing a steep hill.
Only the upward motion contributes to the work.

Planned animations:
Display a circle and a line, color #FFFFFF.
Animate the projection of a vector onto the line.
Use color #FF5733 to highlight the projection vector.

Section: section_2 — The Algebraic Bridge

Lecture lines:
Algebraically, the dot product relates length and angle.
The formula is magnitude times cosine of theta.
It bridges geometry with specific coordinate values.

Planned animations:
Show the matrix multiplication formula, color #FFFFFF.
Transform the matrix elements to reveal the scalar product.
Highlight the final product value in color #33FF57.

Section: section_3 — The Core of Duality: Vectors as Functions

Lecture lines:
View the dot product as a linear function.
A fixed vector acts as a measurement machine.
It transforms any input vector into a scalar.
This perspective introduces the dual space concept.
Imagine a security camera sensing incoming motion.

Planned animations:
Represent vector as an input transformation function.
Animate a grid morphing to visualize the transformation.
Label the input and output spaces with #00FFFF.

Section: section_4 — Visualization: The Dual Nature

Lecture lines:
Visualize the transformation by rotating the vector.
Constant dot products create perpendicular level sets.
These lines reveal the underlying dual landscape.

Planned animations:
Show two intersecting lines, color #FFFFFF.
Rotate one line around the origin.
Animate the change in intersection angle in #FF5733.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Synthesis

Lecture lines:
Dot products translate geometry into precise numbers.
Vectors act as measuring devices for space.
This synthesis completes our view of duality.

Planned animations:
Compile all elements: circle, line, matrix, function.
Arrange them into a final summary diagram.
Color code elements in #FFFFFF and #FF5733 to clarify.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
